detailedLogs.sessionTitle: Comprehensive Assessment by History Taking & Physical Examination
detailedLogs.activityDescription: Conducted two complete head-to-toe comprehensive assessments on adult inpatients. Patient A: 58-year-old male post-laparoscopic cholecystectomy day 2. Conducted systematic interview covering past medical history (hypertension), current medications, pain assessment (PQRST), and full physical exam including surgical port inspection. Patient B: 44-year-old female admitted for acute abdominal pain awaiting diagnostic imaging.
detailedLogs.reflectiveNotesLessonsLearned: What went well: Developed comfortable rapport with both patients and maintained privacy using bedside curtains. Validated subjective pain complaints against objective findings (guarding, vital signs). Challenge: Balancing the detailed questioning without causing patient fatigue; learned to group physical examination steps smoothly to avoid unnecessary repositioning.

detailedLogs.activityDescription: Performed chart audit and bedside verification for two ward patients. Paired subjective statements with objective findings: Patient 1 reported feeling "short of breath when sitting up"; objective findings showed RR 24, shallow chest expansion, SpO2 93% on room air, bibasilar crackles on auscultation. Patient 2 stated pain was "mild 2/10" but exhibited grimacing during transfer, heart rate 94 bpm, and abdominal muscle tensing.
detailedLogs.reflectiveNotesLessonsLearned: Learned that subjective statements do not always tell the full story due to stoicism or fear of analgesics. Objective validation is essential before confirming patient stability.

detailedLogs.sessionTitle: Identifying & Documenting Normal and Abnormal Findings
detailedLogs.activityDescription: Composed standard progress notes using DAR (Data, Action, Response) format for three assigned ward patients. Patient 1: Post-appendectomy day 1; Patient 2: Conservative management of acute pancreatitis; Patient 3: Post-debridement wound with negative pressure therapy. Addressed vital signs, pain ratings, IV infusion rates, surgical dressings, and intake/output balance.
detailedLogs.reflectiveNotesLessonsLearned: Ensured documentation complied with hospital legal standards: objective phrasing without ambiguous abbreviations, timely entry, and clear action-response loops.

detailedLogs.activityDescription: Calculated National Early Warning Score (NEWS) for six assigned surgical patients at 08:00, 12:00, and 14:00. Identified one patient with score escalation from 2 to 5 (tachypnea RR 26, HR 108, BP 98/60, Temp 38.3°C). Documented threshold breach and initiated immediate escalation to medical team within 15 minutes as per protocol.
detailedLogs.reflectiveNotesLessonsLearned: Calculating scores systematically allowed us to catch early sepsis before overt hemodynamic collapse occurred. What to improve: Prepare baseline vitals for quick verbal handoff when dialing the doctor.

detailedLogs.sessionTitle: Differentiating Early Warning Signs & Initiating Timely Interventions
detailedLogs.subCompetencyTitle: Sub-Competency 4: Prevent, Detect and Respond to Complications
detailedLogs.activityDescription: Constructed and delivered two structured SBAR (Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation) escalation reports to preceptor and surgical registrar for patients exhibiting acute changes. Case 1: Suspected pulmonary embolism (hypoxia SpO2 91%, tachycardia, pleuritic chest pain in immobilized orthopedic patient). Case 2: Acute urinary retention post-spinal anesthesia.
detailedLogs.reflectiveNotesLessonsLearned: SBAR structured communication provided an unambiguous framework that eliminated rambling and got immediate physician response. Felt much more confident presenting concise objective data.
